skill.name: implementer
skill.description: Implements one issue inside its own git worktree (.worktrees/issue-N on agent/issue-N), makes the smallest change that satisfies the acceptance criteria, self-checks with the repo's own test/lint/typecheck commands, commits, and prints a JSON report for the orchestrator. Use when the orchestrator launches you with AGENT_FLOW_ROLE=implementer, or the user asks you to implement a specific issue in a worktree.
skill.summary: Implements one scoped issue in an isolated worktree, verifies the change, commits it, and reports evidence.
skill.author: drix10

security_audit.summary: Twenty detections are Markdown backticks around identifiers, file names, examples, or bounded Git commands and are false positives for shell execution. The package installation and repository check instructions are a genuine medium-risk execution surface because project-controlled scripts may run.

remediation.issue: Dependency installation and repository checks can execute project-controlled scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Run installs and checks in a constrained worktree or container, review the lockfile and scripts first, and require approval for networked installation.

content.user_title: Implement Git Issues in Isolated Worktrees
content.value_statement: Issue implementation can drift beyond scope or produce incomplete handoffs. This skill applies focused changes, runs project checks, commits once, and reports structured evidence.
actual_capabilities: Works on one issue inside its assigned Git worktree.
Reads scoped repository guidance before changing code.
Implements acceptance criteria with focused code and test changes.
Runs documented tests, type checks, and lint checks.
Creates one commit and reports changed files, checks, dependencies, and evidence.
limitations: Requires an existing issue, worktree, and repository guidance.
Does not review its own implementation.
Does not modify protected paths or context files.
Stops for ambiguous requirements, blocked operations, or unresolved check failures.

use_cases.title: Implement a Scoped Issue
use_cases.description: Apply a defined issue in a dedicated worktree and produce a review-ready commit.

use_cases.title: Process Orchestrated Work
use_cases.description: Execute one implementation stage and return structured evidence to an agent workflow.

use_cases.title: Address Review Findings
use_cases.description: Correct supported reviewer or quality findings while preserving issue scope.

prompt_templates.title: Implement One Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement issue N in AGENT_FLOW_WORKTREE. Follow its acceptance criteria, run documented checks, create one commit, and return the required report.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Review Corrections
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement issue N and address supported findings in review-rR.json. Verify every correction, preserve scope, commit once, and report evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Handle a Required Dependency
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement issue N with the smallest necessary dependency change. Verify the lockfile, run repository checks, and report the dependency clearly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Implementation that may require a new dependency

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Conflicting Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement issue N while verifying repository claims against source code. Record stale context, escalate contradictions, and provide criterion-level evidence.

output_examples.input: Implement issue 42 and verify the documented checks.
output_examples.output: Ready for review. One commit changes the targeted source and test files. Tests, type checks, and lint checks passed with criterion-level evidence.

output_examples.input: Implement an issue whose acceptance criteria conflict with the current code.
output_examples.output: Human decision required. The report identifies a specification conflict, records the evidence, and recommends the specific decision needed before implementation.

output_examples.input: Address a reviewer finding that contradicts an existing passing test.
output_examples.output: The report disputes the finding with the relevant test evidence and leaves unrelated code unchanged.

best_practices: Provide precise acceptance criteria and the correct assigned worktree.
Keep repository guidance and documented check commands current.
Review the reported commit, check results, dependencies, and stale context before merging.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill for broad refactoring without defined acceptance criteria.
Do not ask it to bypass hooks, protected paths, or branch controls.
Do not treat its report as an independent code review.

faq.question: What input does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires an issue artifact, an assigned Git worktree, and repository guidance such as AGENTS.md.

faq.question: Does it create a commit?
faq.answer: Yes. It stages the scoped worktree changes and creates one commit for the issue.

faq.question: Which checks does it run?
faq.answer: It runs the test, typecheck, and lint commands documented by the repository.

faq.question: Can it add dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes, when the issue requires one. It reports every new dependency for additional risk review.

faq.question: What happens when checks fail?
faq.answer: It retries fixes up to three times, then reports the verbatim failure and requests human direction.

faq.question: Will it edit protected files?
faq.answer: No. It stops and escalates when the required change reaches a protected path or context file.
